answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a vault before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. The contract releases the deposit only after the identity completes a useful task that a counterparty verifies; proven fraud forfeits it. Splitting one operator across a thousand identities then requires a thousand deposits, so Sybil attacks become capital-intensive rather than free. A shared oasis or meadow of public reputation can help users find trusted agents, but the costly, slashable deposit is what raises the attacker’s price.
